51.94898,-7.72573: St. Declan's Oratory With its high-pitched Gables (from which the popular name "The Beannachán), projecting side-walls and lintelled west doorway, this little church may date from the 8th century, though the upper courses of its walls and gables have been rebuilt and the doorway in the north wall is an afterthought. The slate roof was added in 1716 by Dr. Thomas Mills, Bishop of Waterford. This is the reputed burial place if St. Declan, pre-Patrician founder of Ardmore, and is one of the "Stations" on the annual pattern held on his feast day, 24 July, (Journal Royal Society Antiquaries of Ireland, 33 (1903), p366) National MOnument 131

51.95271,-7.84684: Túr an chloig. Mar a bhfuil an túr seo a bhí seangheata theas as bhaile, ar a dtugtaí Caisleán na Tríonóide, go dtí 1777 nuair a tógadh an túr. Bhí an túr ina phríosún go dtí 1837 agus crochadh Cathal Ó Briain agus Cathal Ó Gallchúir, beirt de lucht eiri amach 1798, ó na fuinneoga. D'athchóirigh Comhairle Bhaile Eochaille é le cabhair Bhord Fáilte Éireann agus is músaem agus oifig chuartaíochta anois é. Clock Tower. This tower stands on the site of the old south gate of the town known as Trinity Castle, which it replaces in 1777. It served as a prison until 1837, and in 1798 the patriots Charles O'Brien and Charles Gallagher were hanged from the windows. Restored by Youghal Urban District Council with the help of Bord Failte Eireann, it now serves as a museum and a tourist office.
51.95275,-7.84476: John "Jack" Foley Born in Youghal in 1865, Jack was a storekeeper on the RMS Titanic during her tragic sinking on April 15th 1912. He assisted women and children into lifeboats and helped crew lifeboat No.4 that saved over 50 lives. Jack died in Southampton in 1934.
